article_title: What the performance of multimodal LLMs on a national licensing exam teaches us about occupational therapy education.
citation: Saita Kazuya, Mine Yuichi, Amano Satoru. (2026). What the performance of multimodal LLMs on a national licensing exam teaches us about occupational therapy education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08542-4
title: 60th Japanese National Examination for Occupational Therapists (2025) as an LLM benchmark dataset
description: The 60th JNEOT (February 2025) is a publicly available national licensing exam published by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan, used here as a benchmark for multimodal LLMs. After excluding one officially withdrawn question, "a total of 199 questions were scored, including 177 text-only questions and 22 visually-based questions." Questions span basic sciences and OT-specific content, with 40 practical case-based questions and visual materials such as clinical photographs, CT, MRI and illustrations.
requirements: Official answer keys used as the reference standard; question specialties classified by two researchers with consensus resolution by a third
constraints: The dataset covers a single exam year in Japanese only; categories with small sample sizes (e.g., Rehabilitation Medicine, n = 1) require cautious interpretation
target_learning_goals: assessment of AI capability in professional licensing knowledge
examples: All questions were input into OpenAI o3 between May 3 and 4, 2025, and into the other three models between March 27 and 30, 2025, in a zero-shot manner with no specialized prompt design
key_sources: Saita Kazuya, Mine Yuichi, Amano Satoru. (2026). What the performance of multimodal LLMs on a national licensing exam teaches us about occupational therapy education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08542-4

article_title: Motivation and needs of informal physics practitioners
citation: Shams El-Adawy, Alexandra C. Lau, Eleanor C. Sayre, and Claudia Fracchiolla. (2023). Motivation and needs of informal physics practitioners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19040
title: Joint Network for Informal Physics Education and Research (JNIPER)
description: JNIPER is an APS initiative bringing together physicists who facilitate informal physics learning activities and researchers who investigate their impact, aiming to centralize informal learning efforts. It pursues three goals: creating a supportive foundational community, facilitating research-practice partnerships, and supporting adoption of research-based best practices. Its long-term vision is to "elevate the value and recognition for public engagement in physics" through equity-oriented, culturally competent programming.
requirements: A centralized network connecting researchers and practitioners of informal physics education
constraints: Grounded in research, equity, and culturally competent practices as defined by the JNIPER leadership team
target_learning_goals: community building and adoption of research-based informal physics practices
examples: First initiatives launched Fall 2022 include monthly coffee hours and a JNIPER slack channel where members share resources
key_sources: Shams El-Adawy, Alexandra C. Lau, Eleanor C. Sayre, and Claudia Fracchiolla. (2023). Motivation and needs of informal physics practitioners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19040
